title: 7-round AES-192: schedule-optimized complete-key claim

target.description: AES-192 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 7 rounds. Lucks includes MixColumns in the final round (Section 2.2 footnote). Equivalent subkey L^r=ShiftRows^-1(MixColumns^-1(K^r)); this is not the final-no-MixColumns convention used by FKLSSWW. The schedule supplies W23,W24,W25 from the last round key; two additional equivalent subkey bytes are guessed, followed by the complete-key completion described by analogy to Section 5.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key or known-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: A 2^32-text structure. Printed Step 1 uses (0,0),(1,2),(2,2),(3,1), while Step 2 and the earlier construction use (1,3) for the row-one position; this conflict remains explicit.
assumptions: A wrong integral subkey guess is modeled as passing an eight-bit balance check with probability about 2^-8; repeated checks use the source's heuristic filtering assumptions.
For each initial-key guess, select 32 distinct 256-text sets and test them until a balance check rejects. The accepted material is followed by the stated residual key search.

time.note: The source multiplies 2^32 initial guesses, 2^128 final-key guesses, 2^16 inner guesses and about 2^8 work per test. One basic operation is defined as five byte XORs, five inverse S-box evaluations and one inverse MixColumns evaluation; it is not one S-box lookup or AES encryption.

data.note: The 32 internal test sets are selected from the same 2^32-query structure; they do not multiply the acquisition budget.

memory.note: Dominant storage is the observed ciphertext structure.

preprocessing.note: The paper does not separately price setup for this endpoint.

success.description: Section6 carries over the optimized32-set wrong-tuple model from Section5. Its2^176 candidate-tuple budget yields a separate analyst-derived model estimate of at most about2^-80 for any wrong tuple to pass. That estimate excludes residual full-key identification, uses the source's joint32-test surrogate rather than independent tuples, and leaves the printed state/key-index conflicts unresolved. Complete-key success remains unquantified.

review.scope: AES192 optimized loop and inherited AES25632-test analysis independently rechecked. A model-qualified local union estimate is appended, not a primary success fill. Fixed32 sets per whitening guess and the carried-over per-tuple joint surrogate are required; no adaptive set selection or independence between tuples is assumed. Completion/finite-transcript uniqueness and printed coordinate/index conflicts remain open.

components.description: Chapter7–13 Eq.(3)/Sections3–6: the necessary balance relation holds under the correct hypothesis in the intended Square construction. Existing ShiftRows/printed-coordinate conflicts mean this is not a certification of the literal implementation.
Chapter8/12 Sections3.2/5: source2^-8 for one incorrect terminal tuple to pass a Lambda-set test, conditional on the applicable outer hypotheses. Not full expanded-key recovery success.

Chapter12–13 Sections5–6: the source repeated-test surrogate assigns32 eight-bit tests to a fixed wrong tuple. The AES192 text refers back to that analysis but does not itself report an aggregate2^-80 rate. The separate analyst-derived union component uses this inherited joint surrogate, not an independence claim about distinct tuples. Active-input and BO/state/key-index conflicts remain.

For the source's fixed32 Lambda sets per whitening-key guess, assume its inherited joint wrong-tuple surrogate gives acceptance about at most2^-256 for each incorrect tuple. A union over at most2^32*2^128*2^16=2^176 tuples then gives about2^-80 for any incorrect tuple to pass. No independence between tuples is needed; early stopping cannot enlarge this event. The within-tuple32-test surrogate is an author-model assumption, not proved by distinct sets or valid for adaptive set selection. This is not a validated AES192 implementation bound, does not resolve printed coordinate/key-index conflicts, and excludes remaining full-key completion and finite-transcript identification.

limitations: Costs and success statements are the authors' analytical claims; no complete attack or third-party implementation was executed.

The general BO definition on chapter p8 omits the previous inverse ShiftRows column adjustment for a nonzero target row. For SR(A)(i,j)=A(i,j+s*i), BO input column j and row k require the previous L byte at (k,j+s*k). The surrounding row-0 constructions avoid this adjustment. Independent finite controls check local algebra, not a complete attack repair.

field_conflicts.label: ShiftRows formula and diagram coordinates
field_conflicts.description: Chapterp3 defines left-going SR, B(i,j)=A(i,j+i), but Fig2 and Table1 use right-going coordinates. The later anti-diagonal reaches columns0/2 under the literal left formula and one column under the right diagram. A coherent coordinate convention must be selected before reproducing the printed algorithm. This does not refute the direction-independent integral or establish a standard-key-schedule reflection equivalence.
